Article Title: Porn ads on FB, Insta lure users into fraud: Centre
Article Text:
NCTAU warns of financial fraud via malicious apps disguised as porn apps that take control of devices.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: The National Cybercrime Threat Analytics unit (NCTAU), under the Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre (I4C), has warned users of financial fraud through sideloaded malicious Android apps masquerading as porn apps which, when downloaded, take control of users’ devices by abusing accessibility permissions.NCTAU said misleading Facebook and Instagram ads under the names Night Play, Reloop, Kyss, Riva, Vima, Nexo and Vixa were redirecting users to phishing websites featuring pornographic content, with a prompt to download the APK file from outside the Google Play Store. After installation, the app requests permissions that allow it to install additional applications, enabling fraudsters to take control of the device and commit financial fraud.Some apps also install a VPN, which may be used to route internet traffic pertaining to criminal activity. The app may prevent users from uninstalling it through device settings.Advisory asked users to install apps only from Play Store or trusted stores.
Article Summary: NCTAU warns of financial fraud via malicious apps disguised as porn apps that take control of devices. misleading Facebook and Instagram ads under the names Night Play, Reloop, Kyss, Riva, Vima, Nexo and Vixa were redirecting users to phishing websites featuring pornographic content.

Article Title: Government sounds alarm, ads on Facebook ‌and Instagram found directing users to apps that steal banking passwords and remotely control users' phones
Article Text:
How these apps work, spy and steal

How to uninstall these apps

The government has warned of malicious porn apps on Instagram and Facebook that can completely take over Android phones. In an advisory, National Cybercrime Threat Analytics Unit (NCTAU) said that it has observed a rise in financial frauds perpetrated through malicious Android apps masquerading as pornography apps, circulated through Facebook and Instagram ads. As per the Ministry of Home Affairs advisory, these Android apps are operating under the names "Night Play", "Reloop", "Kyss", “Vimo”, “Rivo”, “Nexo”, “Vixa” and other similar variants.These apps are primarily distributed through advertisements on Facebook and Instagram, which redirect to websites and apps showing pornographic content, where the user is prompted to download an APK file. After installation, the app requests permissions that allow it to install additional apps and by misusing accessibility permission, take control of the users’ device. Some apps also install a VPN, which may be used to route internet traffic pertaining to malicious/criminal activity. As per government warning, these apps can secretly access information stored on users' phones, capture one-time passwords and bank PINs, and transfer money from ​accounts without the owner's knowledge. Not just this, the apps also make it difficult for users to uninstall them through device's normal settings.Distribution: The malicious apps are distributed through pornographic content related advertisements or links majorly on Facebook and Instagram. These ads redirect to phishing websites.Redirection: Ads redirect to phishing websites serving pornographic content. Domains of the website majorly belong to “.live”. Users are persuaded to download and install the APK from sources outside the Google Play Store.App Update: A secondary package gets downloaded and installed on the pretext of an app update, based on permissions abused by the first, initial app.Abuse of Accessibility Permission for device takeover: After installation, the app asks users to grant Accessibility and other sensitive permissions. Once enabled, the malware gains control of the device and continues to run in the background.VPN Installation: Some apps may also install a VPN on the device, thereby routing all internet traffic through attacker-controlled servers. This compromises user's transmitted data, which may subsequently be exploited for malicious or criminal activities.Unauthorized Transactions: Since the malware has the ability to take over the compromised device, installing such apps may lead to financial fraud.METHOD 1: Safe Mode RebootStep 1: Start Your Phone in Safe Mode: Press and hold the Power button. Press and hold Power Off until the Safe Mode option appears. Click OK or Restart in Safe Mode. Wait for the phone to restart. "Safe Mode" will appear at the bottom of the screen.Step 2: Uninstall the App: Open Settings. Go to Apps. Select the suspicious application. Tap Uninstall. Remove any other unknown or related apps.Step 3: Restart Normally: Restart the phone. The device will exit Safe Mode automatically.Second MethodStep 1: Restore the Default Home Screen (If required): Open Settings. Go to Apps → Default Apps → Home App. Select your phone's original launcher (System Launcher, One UI Home, Pixel Launcher, etc.).Step 2: Disable Accessibility Access: Open Settings. Tap Accessibility. Open Installed Services or Downloaded Apps. Select the suspicious application. Turn Accessibility Off.Step 3: Remove Administrator Access: Open Settings. Go to Security or Security & Privacy.Open Device Admin Apps or Device Administrators. If the suspicious app is enabled, select it. Tap Deactivate or Turn Off.Verify the Device: Open Settings > Apps. Confirm that the suspicious application has been removed. If the app cannot be removed or returns after restarting, back up your important data and perform a Factory Reset.
Article Summary: The government has warned of malicious porn apps on Instagram and Facebook that can completely take over Android phones. These apps are primarily distributed through advertisements on Facebook and Instagram, which redirect to websites and apps showing pornographic content. After installation, the app requests permissions that allow it to install additional apps and by misusing accessibility permission, take control of the users’ device.

Article Title: Elon Musk's $60 billion purchase of Cursor that has made Sam Altman 'upset' has an 'indian connection', Aman Sanger
Article Text:
Who is Aman Sanger

Who is Aman Sanger

SpaceX acquire Cursor

OpenAI ends relationship with Cursor

Elon Musk’s $60 billion acquisition of Cursor has put the AI coding startup and its co-founder Aman Sanger in the spotlight, with the deal also drawing attention in India because of Sanger’s family roots. Aman Sanger, who was born in the US to Indian immigrant parents, co-founded Cursor in 2022 after studying computer science at MIT. The AI coding company grew rapidly before being acquired by Musk’s SpaceX, with its founders reportedly receiving billions of dollars in SpaceX shares. The deal has also added another layer to Musk’s rivalry with OpenAI CEO Sam Altman who recently called off its partnership with Cursor.For the 26-year-old Sanger, however, the story goes beyond the Musk-Altman feud, with his Indian family background adding an unexpected connection to the blockbuster AI deal.Born in the US to Indian immigrant parents, Aman Sanger grew up in a household where academic achievement and business success were strongly encouraged. His father, Arvind Sanger, graduated from the Indian Institute of Technology (IIT) Bombay with a B. Tech degree in 1984 before moving to US. He later earned an MBA from Tulane University and built a successful career on Wall Street. His mother, Shilpa became an angel investor through the investment network Golden Seeds.She also took on a business management role at Geosphere Capital.Aman Sanger started coding at the age of 14 and developed an early interest in technology. After enrolling at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT), he studied computer science between 2018 and 2022.Sanger cofounded Cursor, the maker of a popular AI code editing tool, with three friends from the Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT) in 2022. Before starting his own company, Sanger gained experience through internships at Google and Bridgewater Associates. He also launched an AI consultancy before joining fellow MIT students Michael Truell, Sualeh Asif and Arvid Lunnemark to create Cursor in 2022.According to Forbes latest estimate, Aman Sanger has a net worth of over $2.5 billion.Last month, the company was acquired by SpaceX for $60 billion. Forbes estimates that each Cursor cofounder received shares of the rocket maker worth $2.4 billion at the deal's closing.Before the SpaceX acquisition, Cursor claimed to have more than $1 billion in annualized revenue, making it one of the fastest growing AI startups. Today, millions of software developers at enterprises like Nvidia, Adobe, Uber, Shopify and PayPal use Cursor to generate and edit chunks of code.Last week, OpenAI pulled its models out of Cursor, with a proposed shutoff date of November 12, 2026. There is no dispute here about pricing, performance or usage limits. The stated reason is Elon Musk, and OpenAI put that in writing in a public blog post rather than letting it leak out through a support page.OpenAI claims that X, formerly Twitter and now folded into SpaceX, broke the terms of its contract after Musk took over the platform. It also points to sworn testimony this year in which Musk acknowledged that xAI, likewise now part of SpaceX, had violated OpenAI's terms of service. OpenAI added that its forthcoming model, Astra, raises the accountability bar further, which is why it would rather end the arrangement than extend it to a partner it does not trust. It says it gave the maximum notice its contract allows so developers get time to plan.
Article Summary: Aman Sanger was born in the US to Indian immigrant parents. He co-founded Cursor, the maker of a popular AI code editing tool, with three friends from the Massachusetts Institute of Technology in 2022. Forbes estimates that each Cursor cofounder received shares of the rocket maker worth $2.4 billion at the deal's closing.

Article Title: Netflix unveils ‘VOID’, an AI model that can change a movie plot
Article Text:
Netflix

How Netflix VOID works







Netflix has unveiled an AI model that can alter the scene. While this is nothing new, Netflix’s model not just remove objects from video, it understands what should happen next, essentially altering the causality. Most object-removal technology leaves a gap where something used to be and/ or fills it with a plausible-looking background. VOID goes a step further: after erasing an object from a scene, it calculates how the surrounding environment should realistically respond to its absence, and in the process it adjusts the behaviour of other elements in the frame accordingly.The model, called VOID, is a vision-language system designed to edit video footage with a level of contextual awareness that sets it apart from several existing tools.For example, imagine this scenario: A movie director has just wrapped up a multi-million dollar action sequence where the star drives straight into a fiery, head-on collision. The cars explode, debris scatters, and the scene is a wrap.But suddenly, there is request to change the scene: The character survives and drive off into the sunset instead. This would mean costly reshoots or millions spent on computer-generated graphics.Netflix’s VOID can alter the scene and digitally erase the collision, the second vehicle, the smoke, and the flying debris. It will then generate new, realistic footage of pristine pavement, making it look as though the main character simply drove down an empty, peaceful road.The AI’s ‘magic’ lies in its grasp of real-world physics. Let us understand this by a different example. If a video shows a person jumping into a pool and splashing water onto the deck, VOID can completely erase the person. It will then intelligently alter the water and the wet concrete, leaving behind a perfectly still, undisturbed pool as if nobody had ever jumped in.“To train the model, we generate a new paired dataset of counterfactual object removals using Kubric and HUMOTO, where removing an object requires altering downstream physical interactions. During inference, a vision-language model identifies regions of the scene affected by the removed object. These regions are then used to guide a video diffusion model that generates physically consistent counterfactual outcomes,” Netflix said.“Experiments on both synthetic and real data show that our approach better preserves consistent scene dynamics after object removal compared to prior video object removal methods,” the company added.Netflix isn’t keeping this powerful tool locked behind studio doors, and made the VOID model available to the public on the AI platform Hugging Face, allowing anyone to download and use it.While there are already several video-altering tools on the market, such as Runway, DiffuEraser, and ProPainter, the Netflix team claims VOID is vastly superior, as per The Register.
Article Summary: Netflix has unveiled an AI model that can alter the scene. While this is nothing new, Netflix’s model not just remove objects from video, it understands what should happen next, essentially altering the causality. The model, called VOID, is a vision-language system designed to edit video footage with a level of contextual awareness.

Article Title: Kolhapur civic body to carry out patchwork filling using state-of-the-art technology
Article Text:
The Municipal Corporation is piloting the modern ‘Insta Road Patcher’ technology to fill potholes on city roads quickly and durably. A demonstration of this machine, which utilizes GIPSAT bitumen technology, was conducted on the main road between Papachi Tikti and Pan Lane on Monday noon.

Kolhapur:





The Kolhapur municipal corporation is piloting the modern ‘Insta Road Patcher’ technology to fill potholes on city roads quickly and durably. A demonstration of this machine, which utilizes GIPSAT bitumen technology, was conducted on the main road between Papachi Tikti and Pan Lane on Monday noon.The ‘Insta Road Patcher’ tech employs pressure-sensitive material, enabling potholes to be filled within minutes, eliminating the need for heavy machinery such as trucks, dumpers, or large road rollers, and allows road repair work to be carried out with minimal manpower.KMC Commissioner, Dr Rajendra Bharud, MLA Rajesh Kshirsagar, who is the head of state planning commission, and Vishal Shirale, the chairperson of the standing committee, visited the site to inspect the demonstration.This technology utilises a ready-made mixture of bitumen, crushed stone (aggregate), and special chemicals, which does not require heating, and is suitable for use across all seasons and weather conditions. There is no need to wait for the surface to cool down, since the road can be opened to traffic immediately after the repair.Patching a single pothole takes approximately ten minutes. As the repairs made using this technology are capable of lasting at least two years, it can help reduce the costs associated with frequent road repairs, proving useful for small roads and urgent pothole repairs.Filling potholes using traditional methods requires significant manpower, time, and machinery, with the problem of potholes reappearing shortly after repair. Against this backdrop, the IRP-GIPSAT technology could serve as a faster, and more efficient alternative for road repair work.KMC commissioner Dr Rajendra Bharud said, “There are about 1100km of roads in Kolhapur city. Of these, more than 200km are filled every year by the municipal corporation. The concerned company has taken a guarantee of two years for their potholes and if potholes reoccur, then they themselves will repair the road.”
Article Summary: The ‘Insta Road Patcher’ tech employs pressure-sensitive material, enabling potholes to be filled within minutes. It eliminates the need for heavy machinery such as trucks, dumpers, or large road rollers, and allows road repair work to be carried out with minimal manpower.

Article Title: Fraudster uses Raigad SP’s WhatsApp display photo to dupe police staff, seeks Rs 50,000
Article Text:
A cyber fraudster impersonated Raigad SP on WhatsApp, targeting police personnel for money transfers, but the scam attempt was foiled. (AI-generated image)





NAVI MUMBAI: Raigad Cyber Police have registered a case against an unidentified fraudster who allegedly used the WhatsApp Display Picture (DP) of Raigad Superintendent of Police (SP) Anchal Dalal to deceive several police personnel into transferring money.On Thursday, the fraudster sent a message to Raigad SP's reader, PSI Siddheshwar Murkute, asking him to transfer money urgently. Murkute immediately realised that it was a modus operandi commonly used by cyber scammers, as the WhatsApp message was sent from an international number that was not saved in his mobile phone.Thereafter, PSI Murkute learnt that the same scammer had sent similar messages to several Raigad police personnel. Fortunately, no one fell prey to the fraud, as the police personnel were aware of this modus operandi used by cyber fraudsters.Subsequently, PSI Murkute registered an FIR against the unidentified accused under the relevant section of the BNS for the offence of cheating by personation.The complainant, PSI Murkute, said, "I had received the WhatsApp message from an international number and the DP was of Raigad SP Anchal Dalal.The message read, 'I am in a meeting and my mobile is switched off. Immediately transfer Rs 50,000 to my bank account.' I knew the message sender was a scammer. I deliberately replied asking for the bank account number by pretending to send the money. As I received the bank account number from the scammer, it will be useful for the cyber police team to trace the bank account holder. "PSI Murkute added, "One police officer had received a WhatsApp message from the same international number asking to transfer Rs 2,000 by impersonating SP madam and claiming that it was required for filling diesel in the car, and that her mobile battery had drained and she was unable to pay online at the fuel station."API Amol Jadhav of Raigad Cyber Police said, "The cyber scammers use VPNs (Virtual Private Networks) to mask their identity. However, the Internet Protocol (IP) address of the WhatsApp number used by the accused will be obtained to trace the location, and the accused will soon be behind bars."
Article Summary: A cyber fraudster impersonated Raigad SP on WhatsApp, targeting police personnel for money transfers. Fortunately, no one fell prey to the fraud, as the police personnel were aware of this modus operandi used by cyber fraudsters. One police officer received a WhatsApp message from the same international number asking to transfer Rs 2,000 by impersonating SP madam.

Article Title: Nashik City Police appeal to citizens to suggest priority patrolling locations
Article Text:
Nashik

:





In a push toward community-driven policing, the Nashik city police have appealed to residents to suggest key locations, where patrolling should be prioritised. Citizens can submit recommendations in comment sections online, or directly message the CP WhatsApp number 99 233 233 11.Launched on Aug 15, under the direction of CP Sandeep Karnik, nine high-tech ‘One Mobile’ patrolling vans currently operate round-the-clock in two shifts. Designed to supplement ‘Beat Marshals’ and CR mobile units, these squads halt for two hours at a time across 108 pre-mapped locations, including school zones, coaching centres, bustling market by lanes, dark residential streets and ghats.Officials stated that while they might not reach every suggested location every day, every spot shared by citizens was being saved and mapped, assuring them that patrol routes would alternate as the initiative expanded.The state-of-the-art ‘One Mobile’ vehicles are equipped with advanced security features, including 360-degree CCTV surveillance and up to 1 TB of local video storage. Built to seat eight to ten personnel, each van features an integrated internal ladder leading to an upper-deck seating area. This setup functions as a mobile watchtower, allowing officers to monitor large crowds.Currently deployed across nine of the city’s 14 key police stations, these specialised vehicles are designed to respond rapidly to serious crime scenes, crowded events, and emergency calls. Beyond daily crime deterrence and response, officers are undergoing specialised training to leverage these mobile watchtowers for effective crowd management during the upcoming Simhastha Kumbh Mela.
Article Summary: Nashik city police have appealed to residents to suggest key locations, where patrolling should be prioritised. Citizens can submit recommendations in comment sections online, or directly message the CP WhatsApp number 99 233 233 11. Nine high-tech ‘One Mobile’ patrolling vans currently operate round-the-clock in two shifts.

Article Title: Deputy mayor announces incentives for segregating waste
Article Text: Madurai: While Madurai corporation is making source segregation mandatory across all 100 wards, mayor in charge (deputy mayor) T Nagarajan has announced incentives for the households that follow best practices and properly segregate waste for a month in his ward 80.Covering 3,500 households, the drive aims to encourage residents to segregate their daily waste before handing it over to door-to-door collection. Corporation officials, along with NGO Olirum Madurai, distributed four waste bins in different colours to every participating household in the ward.To monitor compliance and digitise the process, a team of students and faculty members, led by dean Shivaranjani, from Sethu Institute of Technology has deployed a tracking system via a mobile app and web portal. The team is fixing QR code stickers on the doors of 3,500 houses. Every morning, sanitation workers will scan the QR codes as they collect the segregated waste, enabling the system to evaluate household compliance and assign daily performance scores based on how well the waste has been segregated.Nagarajan said the incentive will increase awareness and foster cleanliness in the locality.
Article Summary: Madurai corporation is making source segregation mandatory across all 100 wards. Mayor in charge T Nagarajan has announced incentives for households that follow best practices and properly segregate waste for a month in his ward 80. Covering 3,500 households, the drive aims to encourage residents to segregate their daily waste before handing it over to door-to-door collection.

Article Title: ANPR camera system launched in Namakkal district to curb traffic violations
Article Text: NAMAKKAL: An automatic number plate recognition (ANPR) camera system was launched in Namakkal district on Monday to impose fines on traffic violators. The facility was inaugurated at the Namakkal–Salem Road corner junction by district superintendent of police Yadav Krish Ashok.The ANPR system will automatically detect violations such as using mobile phones while driving, riding w-wheelers without helmets and driving without seat belts. Fines will be issued digitally. The penalty amount and receipt will be sent directly to the violator’s registered mobile number.Speaking to reporters, S P Yadav Krish Ashok said, “Road accidents have claimed 348 lives in Namakkal district in the past eight months. Strict monitoring is essential to reduce fatalities. The ANPR camera system will help enforce discipline among motorists. Riders must wear helmets for their own safety and that of their families. Those indulging in reckless stunts will also be closely monitored and penalised.”
Article Summary: The facility was inaugurated at the Namakkal–Salem Road corner junction by district superintendent of police Yadav Krish Ashok. The ANPR system will automatically detect violations such as using mobile phones while driving, riding w-wheelers without helmets and driving without seat belts.

Article Title: ChatGPT is first AI chatbot to face tougher EU rules
Article Text:
ChatGPT is first AI chatbot to face tougher EU rules﻿

ChatGPT will have to comply with tougher safety rules after the EU added it Monday to a list of digital services subject to greater legal scrutiny, a first for an AI chatbot.Brussels also designated Reddit and Roblox as “very large” online platforms, a label that comes with additional obligations and oversight. “ChatGPT, Reddit and Roblox will now be held to a higher standard of scrutiny and accountability in the EU, in line with their large impact on our citizens and society,” EU technology chief Henna Virkkunen said.The designation applies to platforms and search engines with over 45 million monthly active users in the 27-nation bloc, a threshold the three platforms reported meeting, the commission said. The three now have four months to comply with additional obligations under the Digital Services Act, a content law the EU has deployed to rein in Big Tech.
Article Summary: ChatGPT will have to comply with tougher safety rules after the EU added it to a list of digital services subject to greater legal scrutiny. Reddit and Roblox also designated as ‘very large’ online platforms, a label that comes with additional obligations and oversight.

Article Title: Scotland quarry expansion uncovered a 2,000-year-old woman’s grave; archaeologists were stunned by its carefully built stone walls
Article Text:
'Beautifully made' Iron Age burial site containing the skeleton of a woman at a quarry in Sutherland. Image Credit: Highland Archaeological Services (HAS)

Discovery of the 2,000-year-old unique burial in Scotland

What did the Iron Age grave of a woman look like

Further analysis is being carried out on the grave. Image Credit: Highland Archaeological Services (HAS)

Absence of objects in the women’s grave

What can the skeleton reveal about the woman

A nearly 2,000-year-old carefully constructed stone-lined burial containing the remains of a woman has been discovered at a quarry in Sutherland, Scotland, revealing an unexpected glimpse of life and death at that time. Archaeologists from Highland Archaeological Services(HAS) discovered Evelix, near Dornoch, while carrying out work ahead of a planned quarry expansion. The grave was found within an area where evidence of ancient settlement has also been identified, including features that may once have supported timber roundhouses. What caught the archaeologists’ attention was the unusual quality of the stonework. The structure was so neatly built that, at first, the team wondered whether it could have been modern. Instead, the construction style and archaeological evidence pointed towards the Iron Age, with the woman apparently having remained undisturbed for centuries beneath the ground.The discovery was made during archaeological work connected with the planned expansion of the Evelix quarry near Dornoch. According to the BBC, HAS was working for local quarry firm ‘GF Job’ when archaeologists encountered the stone-lined structure.The location was already considered archaeologically important. The Highland Historic Environment Record shows that the wider Evelix area has produced evidence of prehistoric activity, including burial remains, cremation burials, pottery and features linked to earlier settlement. This newly discovered structure stood out because of its carefully constructed stone lining. Instead of looking like a simple hole dug into the ground, it had been deliberately built with substantial masonry. As per the BBC, archaeologist Lynne McKeggie said the team initially thought the structure might be modern because of how well the stonework had been put together. That first impression quickly changed once the remains and other evidence were examined.The structure was dug into sand and measured approximately 3 metres long, 2 metres wide and 1 metre deep, according to the BBC. A small stone staircase formed part of the construction, adding another feature to the burial. Inside, the remains of an individual were found tucked into one corner. The archaeological team believes the individual was a woman and that she may have lain there undisturbed since the Iron Age. The careful construction is one of the most striking parts of the discovery. The stonework had been fitted together so neatly that the archaeologists described the structure as ‘beautifully made.’ Its appearance raises questions about why so much effort was put into creating it.The Highland Historic Environment Record provides an important background to the discovery. The people who built the structure were working without modern machinery, yet they created a substantial stone-lined space with a staircase. The result survived beneath the landscape for roughly two millennia before quarry-related archaeological work exposed it. Earlier archaeological work at the Evelix quarry area had already shown that the landscape contained evidence of prehistoric activity.The burial does not appear to have contained a collection of obvious grave goods. The BBC reported that no objects were found inside the structure, although archaeologists did identify a large quantity of animal bone. The absence of objects does not make the discovery less significant. In fact, it leaves more questions about the purpose of the structure and the circumstances surrounding the woman's burial. The animal remains may provide useful evidence as further analysis takes place. The construction itself can offer clues about the importance of the site to the people who used it. The wider archaeological record for Evelix also shows that prehistoric burials and settlement activity had previously occurred in the area.The remains could eventually provide a much more personal picture of the woman who was buried at the site. BBC reports that GF Job is funding further analysis of the human remains. Specialists will study the skeleton in greater detail, with the aim of learning more about the individual and the circumstances surrounding the burial. For now, many details remain unknown. Her exact age, background and life story cannot be established simply from the discovery itself. Those answers will depend on the scientific examination still to come. Archaeologists are using photographs and 3D scans to preserve information about the structure and the position of the remains.Once the further analysis has been carried out, the skeleton will be made available to Treasure Trove Scotland for potential allocation to a museum. What began as archaeological work ahead of a modern quarry expansion has revealed a carefully constructed resting place that had remained hidden for around 2,000 years. The woman's identity may never be known, but the grave itself has survived as a quiet reminder of the care and effort that people in Iron Age Sutherland could invest in remembering their dead.
Article Summary: Archaeologists from Highland Archaeological Services(HAS) discovered Evelix, near Dornoch, while carrying out work ahead of a planned quarry expansion. The structure was dug into sand and measured approximately 3 metres long, 2 metres wide and 1 metre deep. Inside, the remains of an individual were found tucked into one corner. Archaeologists believe the individual was a woman and that she may have lain there undisturbed since the Iron Age.

Article Title: In 2024, England turned old fishing nets into a 16-metre footbridge; the 3.5-tonne structure needs smaller foundations and less maintenance than a conventional bridge
Article Text:
The project used modular blocks, which mostly can be placed by hand, instead of traditional reinforced-concrete retaining walls. The blocks fit together like a Lego system, with little or no mortar needed.

Lego-like construction system

A journey by land and sea

Lower carbon footprint, less maintenance

Old fishing nets seldom find a second life. But in Kent, England, the nets are being turned into something much more ambitious. The used nets have been transformed to make a 16-metre-long footbridge to carry people over a marina entrance with minimal environmental impact during construction. Media reports from 2024 say that the Environment Agency built an innovative bridge at Twyford Marina in Yalding using recycled materials, lightweight engineering, and a construction method to reduce the amount of concrete used. The 16-metre bridge is part of the Medway Valley Walk and offers pedestrians a new route across the entrance to Twyford Marina. It also makes it easier for boats to enter and leave the marina. The bridge deck and main structure are made of fibre-reinforced polymer, or FRP, from recycled old fishing nets. The material is a blend of strength and light weight and is particularly useful in a challenging construction location. According to reports, the completed bridge is much lighter at 3.5 tons than many traditional structures of a similar size. The weight reduction also allowed engineers to use smaller support foundations.The innovation is not only the bridge itself. If we go by the GOV UK website, the project used modular blocks, which mostly can be placed by hand, instead of traditional reinforced-concrete retaining walls. The blocks fit together like a Lego system, with little or no mortar needed. According to experts, this method requires less reinforced concrete, making construction simpler and potentially reducing the project's carbon footprint. Lighter materials and smaller footings also allowed the bridge to be constructed in a site where it would have been difficult to deliver large construction equipment.The bridge's journey to Kent was no less strange. According to the GOV UK website, the deck was built in the Netherlands before being shipped to Nottinghamshire and fitted with handrails. From there, the 3.5-ton structure was transported by road to Yalding. Her last voyage was by barge up the River Medway. When the bridge reached the marina, a crane set it in place. The bridge is now open to the public.According to the 2024 report, the Environment Agency anticipates that the recycled FRP structure will require less maintenance than a conventional bridge built from traditional materials. It’s also lighter, which means the foundations it needs are smaller. Less construction material is required, and fewer emissions are generated. In the current scenario, the project shows how infrastructure is a place where pragmatic engineering and the circular economy meet. The project has given a new lease of life to discarded fishing nets, giving them a useful second life in a structure designed to serve walkers and boat users for years. On an ordinary journey, you now pass through an extraordinary piece of environmental engineering at Twyford Marina, made from waste that once belonged to the sea.What are your views on this? Article Title: Nominee vs legal heir: What is the difference and who has claim on assets? All you need to know
Article Text:

Who is a Nominee?



Who is a Legal Heir?

Difference between a Nominee and a Legal heir

Aspect Nominee Legal Heir Role Custodian Owner Transfer of Assets Can be done without any legal formalities. Requires testamentary documents for proof of ownership. Powers No power to transact, use, or transfer assets. Power to use and transact assets as an owner. Appointment Owner can appoint anyone, but some institutions specify certain conditions. Determined by succession/personal laws. Legal Right Cannot contest ownership legally. Can contest ownership in a court of law.

When individuals open bank accounts, invest in mutual funds, or buy insurance, they are often asked to name a nominee.However, many people mistakenly assume that the nominee automatically inherits the assets. In reality, the nominee is not always the final recipient — the ownership rights belong to the legal heir, reported ET.Understanding the distinction between these two is essential to ensure that your wealth is passed on to the intended beneficiaries.A nominee acts as a temporary custodian of the deceased person’s assets.The nominee’s role is limited to holding and managing the assets until they are legally transferred to the rightful heirs.According to ET, the nominee cannot sell, trade, or make any transactional decisions about the assets.The account or policy owner can appoint anyone — family, friends, or acquaintances — as a nominee, though financial institutions often prefer close family members.In some cases, the nominee and the legal heir can be the same person, which helps in ensuring a smoother transfer of assets.The legal heir or beneficiary is the rightful owner of the assets once the original holder passes away.To claim ownership, the legal heir must produce valid documents such as a will or other testamentary proof.If there is no will — a situation known as dying intestate — the heir is determined as per the country’s succession or personal laws, reported ET.While a nominee can initially access the assets, only the legal heir can claim them permanently or challenge ownership in court.Experts quoted by ET emphasise that having clarity on this difference helps avoid disputes and ensures that the savings reach the intended family members or beneficiaries.Therefore, it is advisable to regularly update both nominees and wills to align with one’s estate planning goals.
Article Summary: A nominee acts as a temporary custodian of the deceased person’s assets. The legal heir or beneficiary is the rightful owner of the assets once the original holder passes away. To claim ownership, the legal heir must produce valid documents such as a will.

How Jeevan Pramaan simplifies pensioner verification



Every year, lakhs of pensioners across India must prove that they are still alive to continue receiving their pension. This verification, known as the Life Certificate or Digital Life Certificate (DLC), is a crucial and mandatory step in ensuring that pension payments are made only to eligible recipients, preventing fraud and misuse.Traditionally, this process involved visiting the bank or pension office in person, standing in long queues, and submitting a signed paper certificate. However, with the government’s focus on digitisation and technological advancement, this process has become much simpler, faster, and more convenient. Pensioners can now submit their certificates digitally from the comfort of their homes using Jeevan Pramaan, a secure, user-friendly, and Aadhaar-based platform.A Life Certificate is an official document that confirms a pensioner is alive. Without it, pension payments are automatically paused by the pension disbursing agency. This verification is essential for preventing fraudulent claims and ensuring that pensions reach the rightful beneficiaries.The Digital Life Certificate (DLC), also known as Jeevan Pramaan, is an advanced biometric-enabled version of the traditional paper certificate.Introduced by the Government of India, it uses Aadhaar-based biometric authentication using either fingerprint or iris scan to verify a pensioner’s identity. Once verified, a digital certificate is automatically generated and shared with authorised pension disbursing agencies.This online process eliminates the need for physical verification, providing elderly pensioners with a simpler and more accessible way to maintain their pension benefits.According to PIB, The submission of the Life Certificate is mandatory for all pensioners who wish to continue receiving their pension without interruption. For the year 2025, the standard submission period is betweenTo make the process more comfortable for the elderly, the government allows pensioners aged 80 years and above to begin the submission process earlier, from 1 October 2025. This extended window gives senior citizens more time and flexibility to complete the procedure without facing last-minute difficulties.The Jeevan Pramaan process involves two main steps: registering the biometric device and generating the digital certificate.Before using the service, pensioners or operators must register their biometric device such as a fingerprint or iris scanner. During registration, the user provides their Aadhaar number and mobile number, after which an OTP (One-Time Password) is sent to their mobile. After entering the OTP, they must provide their name and email ID before scanning their fingerprint or iris.Once authentication is complete, the system confirms that device registration was successful, allowing the user to move to the next step.In this step, the pensioner enters personal details such as Aadhaar number, mobile number, name, PPO number, pension type, sanctioning authority, disbursing agency, and bank account details. The system also asks whether the pensioner has remarried or is re-employed.After entering all details, the pensioner scans their fingerprint or iris using the registered biometric device. Upon successful authentication, the Digital Life Certificate is generated, and an SMS acknowledgment with the Jeevan Pramaan Certificate ID is sent to the registered mobile number.This certificate is automatically stored in the Life Certificate Repository, accessible anytime to both pensioners and pension agencies.Once the Digital Life Certificate is created, it can be electronically delivered to the concerned Pension Disbursing Agency (PDA). PDAs can log in to the Jeevan Pramaan portal to view, verify, or download the certificate directly.Pensioners can also download a PDF copy of their certificate by visiting the Jeevan Pramaan website and entering their Pramaan ID or Aadhaar number. This ensures transparency and easy access for future reference.The government provides several options to submit the Life Certificate, allowing pensioners to choose the method that suits them best.Pensioners who prefer traditional methods can visit their bank branch or a Citizen Service Centre (CSC) to submit their Life Certificate physically. Trained staff at these centres assist pensioners in verifying their details and completing the process.For those unable to travel due to age or health issues, India Post Payments Bank (IPPB) offers a doorstep banking service. Pensioners can schedule an appointment, and an IPPB representative will visit their home to complete the submission using biometric authentication. This service is available for both IPPB and non-IPPB account holders.For pensioners comfortable with technology, the Jeevan Pramaan portal provides a completely online process. By visiting https://jeevanpramaan.gov.in, pensioners can submit their Digital Life Certificate using a computer, laptop, or smartphone equipped with a fingerprint or iris scanner.The system uses the Aadhaar platform to authenticate biometric details. Once verification is successful, a Digital Life Certificate is generated and stored in a secure online repository. Pension disbursing agencies can then directly access the certificate, removing the need for physical paperwork.The UMANG (Unified Mobile Application for New-age Governance) app offers another easy option. Pensioners can download the app from the Google Play Store, search for “Jeevan Pramaan,” and select “Generate Life Certificate.”After entering the necessary details such as Aadhaar number, PPO number, and type of pension, pensioners must authenticate themselves using biometric verification. The app then generates a Digital Life Certificate (DLC), which is automatically shared with the pension disbursing authority.All pensioners who receive government, defence, or private sector pensions through authorised disbursing agencies are required to submit their Life Certificate every year. This includes:Failure to submit the certificate within the stipulated period may result in temporary suspension of pension payments until verification is completed.To ensure a smooth submission process, pensioners should keep certain details and documents ready. These include:Having these details ready helps to avoid delays or errors during authentication, whether submitting online or offline.Yes, an Aadhaar number or Virtual ID (VID) is mandatory to generate a Digital Life Certificate. The entire Jeevan Pramaan system is based on Aadhaar authentication, which ensures accuracy and prevents fraud. Pensioners must make sure their Aadhaar is linked with their mobile number and bank account before attempting to generate the certificate.The Digital Life Certificate is fully valid and legally recognised under the Information Technology Act. Pension disbursing authorities across India accept it as an official document, equivalent to the traditional paper-based life certificate.Its biometric verification system makes it secure and tamper-proof, reducing the chances of wrongful pension disbursal or misuse of pension funds.Before the introduction of Jeevan Pramaan, pensioners often faced difficulties in submitting their certificates, especially those with health problems or limited mobility. The digital system has removed these challenges, allowing pensioners to submit their verification anytime and anywhere.By integrating biometric technology and Aadhaar authentication, Jeevan Pramaan has streamlined pension management, improving efficiency for both pensioners and government departments. It also enhances transparency and ensures that genuine beneficiaries receive payments on time.

This verification is essential for preventing fraudulent claims and ensuring that pensions reach the rightful beneficiaries. The Digital Life Certificate (DLC), also known as Jeevan Pramaan, is an advanced biometric- enabled version of the traditional paper certificate.

Article Title: How to get your CIBIL credit score without a PAN card
Article Text:
Your credit score is a three-digit number that reflects your creditworthiness and repayment capacity.

What is a CIBIL score?

How to get your CIBIL Credit score without a PAN Card

Factors affecting your CIBIL score

CIBIL credit score : Understanding your creditworthiness is pivotal in today's financial landscape, especially when seeking loans or credit cards. The Credit Information Bureau (India) Limited, commonly known as CIBIL, plays an important role in this regard by providing credit scores to borrowers.According to ET, credit score helps banks make informed decisions about extending credit cards and loans. Your credit history influences your CIBIL score , which is calculated using a special method.Your CIBIL score is a three-digit number that reflects your creditworthiness and repayment capacity. Ranging from 300 to 900, a higher score indicates a stronger likelihood of loan approval. Banks and financial institutions use this score to assess the risk associated with lending money.1. Go to the official CIBIL website and click on 'Personal CIBIL score,' then 'Get Your Free CIBIL score.' Follow the link provided and fill in all the required details.2. If you don’t have a PAN Card, you can use an alternative identification such as Passport, Voter ID, Driver’s License, or Ration Card. Enter the number of the chosen ID.3. Provide your date of birth, PIN code, and select your state. Finally, enter your mobile number and click on ‘Accept and Continue’.4. Authenticate your identity by entering the OTP (One-Time Password) delivered to your mobile device on the next screen. Click 'Continue' to proceed.5. Choose whether you want to link the device with your account. Select 'Yes' or 'No' based on your preference.6. Upon successful registration, you will see a page confirming that 'You have successfully registered!'7. Click on ‘Go to Dashboard’ to access and view your CIBIL score.The factors influencing the new CIBIL score, as stated on the CIBIL website, include:1. Depth of credit: This refers to the duration of your existing credit history, calculated from the opening date of your oldest credit account.2. Long-term trend of outstanding balances: The overall trend of outstanding balances over time affects your score.3. Transaction history on credit cards: How you manage transactions on your credit cards impacts your score.4. Ratio of actual repayment amount to total amount due: This ratio indicates your repayment behavior and influences your score accordingly.5. Number of new accounts opened and number of accounts closed: Opening or closing accounts can affect your score, so managing these actions wisely is important.
Article Summary: Your CIBIL score is a three-digit number that reflects your creditworthiness and repayment capacity. Article Title: Tata to develop air taxi in India; expected to take flight in 2 years

The engagement also creates opportunities to extend support across sensor fusion-based navigation software, industrial and structural design, and airworthiness test support.Sarla Aviation co-founder and CEO Adrian Schmidt said: “Building a new class of aircraft is not simply an engineering challenge. Advanced air mobility is no different, and Sarla Aviation's vision for Shunya reflects the ambition driving this transformation. Initiatives like this create opportunities to apply expertise built across aerospace, mobility and digital technologies to entirely new aviation platforms. ”Jayaraj Rajapandian, Tata Elxsi head of aerospace, added: “Shunya is a reminder of how quickly aerospace innovation is evolving in shaping the Technology landscape in India. We are excited to work alongside Sarla Aviation as they take this vision forward and contribute to the next phase of its journey. ”Beyond Shunya, the partnership is expected to help strengthen capabilities relevant to logistics, air ambulance services and defence-related applications. By bringing together expertise from aerospace and mobility, Tata Elxsi aims to help build the foundations for advanced air mobility platforms in the country.

Article Title: Apple Mac minis and Mac Studios have disappeared from store shelves in many countries, and how this shortage links to OpenAI and Anthropic
Article Text:
OpenAI reportedly bought tens of thousands of Apple Macs for AI

Why Mac mini and Mac Studio are attracting AI developers

OpenClaw craze adds to Mac mini demand in China

Apple’s Mac mini and Mac Studio computers have become increasingly difficult to find in several markets, and the AI boom may be playing a surprising role in the shortage. According to a report by The information, OpenAI has bought tens of thousands of Mac minis and Mac Studios for work involving AI agents and reinforcement learning, while Anthropic has reportedly rented Mac minis through Amazon Web Services for similar tasks. At the same time, developers and consumers are increasingly turning to Apple's compact computers to run AI agents locally. The demand has been particularly visible in China, where the popularity of OpenClaw has reportedly pushed Mac mini stocks down and prices up.According to The Information, OpenAI has spent several months buying tens of thousands of Mac minis and Mac Studios. The computers are reportedly being used for reinforcement learning and AI agents that can interact with computers.Anthropic has also reportedly been using Mac minis, although through a different route. The Claude maker is said to have rented the machines through Amazon Web Services for similar AI work.The demand highlights an unusual role for Apple's small desktop computers. Macs are not replacing Nvidia's powerful GPUs for training the largest AI models. Instead, they can be useful for another growing area of artificial intelligence: AI agents that interact with regular computer environments.Such agents can look at a screen, use a browser, click buttons and repeatedly attempt tasks. Running many such sessions can require a large number of computers.One reason is Apple's unified memory architecture. Instead of keeping CPU and GPU memory completely separate, Apple silicon allows different parts of the system to access a common pool of memory. High-memory Mac configurations can therefore run some local AI models that may struggle to fit within the dedicated memory available on consumer graphics cards.The machines also offer developers a complete macOS environment. That can matter when an AI agent needs to learn how to operate software and perform tasks on a desktop rather than simply process information in a data centre.Demand is not limited to large AI companies. The Mac mini has also become a popular choice among people running OpenClaw, an open-source AI agent. The trend has been particularly visible in China, where running OpenClaw has become known as “raising a lobster”, a reference to the project's mascot.According to the South China Morning Post, Mac minis were selling out at retailers in parts of China earlier this year. Some sellers with remaining stock were reportedly charging hundreds of yuan above normal prices.The Mac mini's appeal for OpenClaw is also linked to security. AI agents can require extensive permissions to control a computer, access information and carry out tasks. Running such software on a person's main computer could create risks if permissions are incorrectly configured or third-party tools contain malicious code.That has encouraged some users to run AI agents on a separate machine. The Mac mini's small size and ability to run AI workloads locally have made it one option for such setups.
Article Summary: OpenAI reportedly bought tens of thousands of Apple Macs for AI. The computers are reportedly being used for reinforcement learning and AI agents that can interact with computers. The Mac mini has also become a popular choice among people running OpenClaw, an open-source AI agent.

Article Title: In 2025, researchers used fired clay bricks and eggshell waste, reducing energy consumption for heating and cooling by 50%, turning food waste into useful building material
Article Text:
AI generated Image for representational purpose

How eggshell waste was added to clay bricks

10% eggshell bricks showed the biggest drop in heat transfer

The waste problem is part of the attraction

A pile of discarded eggshells could have a surprising second life: inside building bricks. In 2025, researchers in Egypt tested fired clay bricks made with eggshell waste. As part of the study, researchers then found that the right amount of eggshell powder can significantly reduce heat transfer through the material. The study found that bricks containing 10% eggshell waste and fired at 1,100°C recorded a 50% reduction in thermal conductivity compared with ordinary clay bricks. Researchers also found that the thermal diffusivity and thermal effusivity also fell by about 30%.The researchers collected eggshells, cleaned and dried them, then ground them into powder. The powder was mixed with clay from Egypt's Kharga Oasis. Researchers used different proportions of eggshells ranging from 1% to 10%.The study found that eggshells changed the internal structure of the bricks. During high-temperature firing, calcium carbonate in the eggshells breaks down and releases carbon dioxide. This process helps create pores inside the material.The strongest thermal result came from the brick containing 10% eggshell waste. Compared to the untreated clay brick, the researchers recorded a 50% drop in thermal conductivity, meaning less heat could pass through the material.Thermal diffusivity and thermal effusivity each fell by about 30%, the research found.The results, researchers believe, can have significance for buildings in hot climates, where walls absorb and transfer heat from the outside into indoor spaces. Bricks with more air spaces can slow heat movement because air is a poor conductor of heat. The researchers found that adding eggshell waste changed the brick's internal structure and density, creating conditions that improved its insulation performance.The study also points to another potential benefit: recycling eggshells instead of sending them to landfills. The researchers noted that more than 110 billion eggshells are estimated to end up in landfills worldwide. Turning some of this waste into construction material could give it a useful purpose while reducing the need for some raw materials.
Article Summary: Researchers in Egypt tested fired clay bricks made with eggshell waste. Found that the right amount of eggshell powder can significantly reduce heat transfer through the material. Researchers collected eggshells, cleaned and dried them, then ground them into powder. powder was mixed with clay from Egypt's Kharga Oasis.

Article Title: In 2024, Netflix told shareholders it needed no partners; now its co-CEO Greg Peters says outside deals are ‘very promising’
Article Text:
Netflix co-CEO Greg Peters

"very promising,"

"If we see additional deals that similarly serve our members, that work for our partner, that work for us, we'll certainly consider them,"

Netflix shifts its tone on partnerships

Other streaming giants are also racing to bundle

"The thing that matters is that when you turn on the TV, what app are you opening for the next three hours?"

Two years ago, Netflix told its shareholders that the companyThis made it clear that the streaming giant saw little need to feature rival services within its own app. Now, that position has softened considerably. Speaking on its latest earnings call, Netflix co-chief executive Greg Peters described the early results of a new partnership with French broadcaster TF1 asand signalled the company is open to striking similar deals elsewhere.Peters said.Netflix's moves have been more subtle than some of its rivals, but that could soon change. In June, the company began streaming TF1 in its French markets, including a live feed of TF1 networks and on-demand programs. It marked Netflix's first arrangement of its kind, and it appears to be a test case for something larger.A report by The New York Times cited three people familiar with the discussions, who said Netflix executives recently held talks with NBCUniversal and the Fox Corporation about bringing Peacock and Fox One to Netflix's platform.However, the people warned that no deal is imminent, and that it remains unclear whether Netflix would absorb the outside content directly into its own service, as in a recent YouTube-Peacock arrangement, or instead act more as a retailer, similar to how Amazon Prime Video operates.Netflix is not alone in this pivot. For years, Amazon has persuaded tens of millions of people to use its Prime Video app to subscribe to other services, like HBO Max or Apple TV, and to watch shows like "The Pitt" or "Ted Lasso" from within the retail giant's digital walls. Now, other streaming leaders are sprinting to catch up.YouTube and Roku are racing to become one-stop shops for all the content people watch on their televisions. People who pay for a commercial-free YouTube tier, for example, will soon have access to Peacock content like "The Traitors" and "Sunday Night Football" as part of a recent deal between the two companies.The push underscores a broader competitive shift among the titans of streaming television. Companies that were once laser-focused on gaining new subscribers are now far more concerned with keeping those people watching as much as possible, and cancelling as little as possible. What were once described as the streaming wars have effectively morphed into bundling wars. The biggest streaming firms are no longer content to just have the most subscribers; they also want to be the main entry point to everything streaming has to offer.Jonathan Carson, chief executive of Antenna, a subscription research firm, told the NYT.Consumers already appear receptive to managing their subscriptions through a single platform. Over the last three years, subscriptions made via third-party platforms like Amazon, Roku or YouTube have grown roughly 60 per cent, according to Antenna, with about a third of all new subscriptions now purchased this way.
Article Summary: Netflix's new partnership with French broadcaster TF1 is "very promising," says co-CEO Greg Peters. The company has also held talks with NBCUniversal and the Fox Corporation about bringing Peacock and Fox One to Netflix's platform. The push underscores a broader competitive shift among the titans of streaming television.

Article Title: Fireflies AI co-founder and CEO Krish Ramineni shares the ‘biggest problem’ with Google, Microsoft meeting assistants and how he aims to beat them
Article Text:
Fireflies AI co-founder and CEO Krish Ramineni

Google, Microsoft have ‘closed ecosystem’ problem

Shift from notetaker to ‘action-taker’ and India-centric features

'Fireflies keeping the highest bar in security and privacy'

When tech giants like Google and Microsoft roll out built-in AI features, the immediate reaction of many users is often to write off independent AI startups. This is the billion-dollar question every founder faces. But for Fireflies.ai co-founder and CEO Krish Ramineni, what these tech titans view as their greatest strength is exactly where agile startups are finding their ultimate competitive advantage. The US-based company is betting on cross-platform flexibility, deeper workflow integrations and several India-first features to stay ahead of the competition.Talking with The Times of India tech, Ramineni addressed the long-standing challenge of competing against Silicon Valley's tech giants, highlighting that ecosystem fragmentation remains the single biggest flaw in Big Tech's meeting assistants. While proprietary AI solutions from Google or Microsoft are locked into their own environments, modern professionals and their external clients operate across a scattered mix of calling tools throughout the workday.“This is something that I [have been] thinking about every night for the last five years, even before we really took off. There’s a multi-pronged approach to this one. The simple answer is: knowledge is fragmented.If you're using Google's AI, it’s only going to work on Google and not on [Microsoft] Teams, or Zoom,” Ramineni told TOI.“So, fragmentation is actually something that we can address where you have one AI that works across all platforms and people want consistency,” he added, explaining that employees may have a zoom meeting now; then an hour later, you have a meeting on Teams. And then, a Google Meet meeting.“You need one platform that brings it together. Also, the AI that you use or the video conferencing tools that you use might be different from what your clients or your customers use. So that alone makes it a very compelling value proposition for why people are using Fireflies.ai and continue to use it,” he explained.He further noted that the team has had a lot of time to make the core experience better for a lot of larger companies. “We have to go 10 layers deeper on the quality of the product. We can't just say, ‘Okay, it's good enough to bundle it’. We have to prove our metal every day”, he said, pointing out that the platform now has over 120 different integrations and a rich API that makes it accessible for people.Fireflies is actively expanding into a multi-product company designed to handle broader knowledge work before, during and after meetings. Earlier this month, the company expanded its features by launching an email assistant.With this, the platform is evolving from passive transcription to executing follow-up tasks, such as creating presentation slide decks, drafting post-call emails, building project memos, and pinging colleagues on Slack.Over the coming year, Fireflies plans to introduce roughly a dozen new capabilities outside standard meeting notes, including autonomous voice agents designed to attend and conduct preliminary screening interviews on a user's behalf.When talking about India-centric features, Ramineni explained that in India, app adoption is one of the highest.“One thing I'm immediately seeing is the use of our mobile app in India, especially because people are having a lot of in-person meetings. And the mobile app has been a big adoption where they're able to just pull out Firefly's hit and record on it. And that's been something we're seeing uniquely,” he said.“We've constantly been increasing beyond Hindi to other languages as well. Today, Firefly supports almost 100 different languages and continues to improve on that aspect. And then, from our own point of view, we’re announcing this gradually but we want to create plant pricing plans specific for India that are more geo-friendly,” Ramineni told TOI.When asked about AI regulation, Ramineni said that the company has different AI policies in different markets.“I want to take a particular example here, which is around call recording consent. It's different in many markets, and we've always taken that position that consent is necessary. It's mandatory in many places, and you should make it explicit,” he said, adding that there may be certain countries that don't have consent-related policy, but we're going to be proactive and do what is the right thing.He explained that the company takes the “highest standard” and follows that. “Be it anywhere. We’ve decided not to set different standards for different countries.”Fireflies.ai is used by over 20 million people and 1 million organisations, including 75% of the Fortune 500. According to the company, it has processed more than 7 billion meeting minutes and integrates with 100+ workplace tools.
Article Summary: Fireflies.ai co-founder and CEO Krish Ramineni: 'Knowledge is fragmented. If you're using Google's AI, it’s only going to work on Google and not on [Microsoft] Teams, or Zoom,’ he told The Times of India tech.

Article Title: No AI in GTA 6 actually means no generative AI, and there is a difference
Article Text:
GTA 6 has no generative AI, but its traffic, pedestrians and police still run on AI (Image via Rockstar Games)

Vice City was built street by street, not prompted into existence

No microtransactions in GTA 6 , but the Ultimate Edition still costs $20 more

Rockstar has confirmed that Grand Theft Auto 6 will launch with no generative AI and no way to spend real money inside the game. Rob Nelson, co-studio head at Rockstar North, gave both answers during a preview visit to the studio's Edinburgh headquarters, speaking to Kinda Funny Games hosts Andy Cortez and Greg Miller. Miller says he put the AI question point-blank. The answer was no.That needs unpacking, because "no AI" and "no generative AI" are not the same sentence. Grand Theft Auto has run on artificial intelligence since the series went 3D. Traffic that reroutes around a crash, pedestrians who react to a drawn weapon, police who coordinate a chase across three blocks: all of that is AI, and all of it is still in GTA 6. What Rockstar is ruling out is the newer stuff, the generative tools that write dialogue, spin up textures or fill a map with machine-made assets.Take-Two chairman Strauss Zelnick said much the same in February, describing Rockstar's worlds as constructed street by street rather than generated. The numbers support that. GTA 6 is reported to carry well over 600,000 animations, against roughly 55,000 in GTA 5 and around 300,000 in Red Dead Redemption 2. That is hand-authored work at a scale that partly explains why this game has taken 13 years.The distinction matters right now because generative AI has become a reputational hazard.Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 and Arc Raiders both took heat from players who spotted machine-generated elements. Rockstar answering the question directly, before launch, closes that argument off early.Cortez asked separately whether players could buy anything with real money in-game and was told there is no monetisation. That is a meaningful commitment for a single-player release, though it comes with an asterisk. The standard edition is $79.99 and the Ultimate Edition is $99.99, and the extra $20 buys cosmetic packs, cars, guns and shops including the Electric Fang tattoo parlour and the Stock 305 clothing store. Rockstar has confirmed standard buyers can upgrade later. Content behind a paywall is still content behind a paywall, just sold once instead of continuously.Rockstar refused to say anything about the next version of GTA Online, which is where Shark Cards have generated real money for over a decade. Nobody expects that model to disappear.The interest is already visible. Sensor Tower estimates pre-orders climbed 436 percent on 27 August, the day the Netflix Extended Look aired, with PlayStation up 606 percent against 127 percent for Xbox.GTA 6 launches 19 November for PS5 and Xbox Series X/S.
Article Summary: GTA 6 launches 19 November for PS5 and Xbox Series X/S. Standard edition is $79.99 and the Ultimate Edition is $99.99. Extra $20 buys cosmetic packs, cars, guns and shops including the Electric Fang tattoo parlour and the Stock 305 clothing store.

We beat GTA 6!” According to the company, the version 2.0 overhaul prioritises user accessibility, significantly cutting down initial installation friction while adding multi-user collaboration tools and deeper cross-platform automation.“Today we released by far the largest update in the history of OpenClaw. It was built by 933 contributors, including 569 first-time contributors, and is composed of over 16,000 pull requests,” the company said, adding, “This update touches every part of OpenClaw, including installation, messaging, memory, skills, models, automations, the browser and native apps, plugins, security, and a very long tail of fixes. ”According to the company, OpenClaw 2.0 simplifies initial onboarding by removing cumbersome manual configurations.For example, rather than requiring complex upfront setup, the software automatically discovers existing AI credentials and local frameworks on a device, including API keys, Claude, ChatGPT, Codex logins, and local runners like LM Studio and Ollama.Additionally, users can start interacting with their personal AI agent immediately, finishing secondary configuration settings through conversational prompts. Desktop deployment across Linux, Windows, and macOS has been streamlined, while mobile apps on iOS and Android now feature a simplified permissions and device pairing flow.“Before this update, we had shipped 106 releases in 230 days, most within a day or two of the one before them, so going nearly seven weeks without shipping was not normal for us. The release cadence slowed, but development moved in the opposite direction because our team was growing, and the increased volume and pace of work outgrew both the foundation of OpenClaw and the process we used to ship it, so we reworked both at the same time,” the company added.The primary browser portal has been completely overhauled into a centralised productivity workspace. The new web dashboard launches straight into active dialogues with the user’s AI agent, consolidating approvals, files, system preferences, and chat threads into one unified view. The new navigation features include pinned chat threads, structured session grouping, unified system search, and real-time Markdown rendering.Version 2.0 also expands the platform’s real-world agentic workflow capabilities allowing users to configure autonomous routines that monitor incoming emails, flag urgent communications, and forward push alerts directly through messaging apps like Telegram. The assistant can also pull information across disparate channels, such as locating a retail invoice in an inbox and automatically replying with the requested info over iMessage.

Article Text:
What Anthropic told affected users

The malware behind the attacks

How Anthropic is responding

What Anthropic is telling users to do

AI giant Anthropic has issued a warning to Claude users after discovering that infostealer malware is hijacking active login sessions to access accounts and drain usage. According to a report by Bleeping Computers, the company said that the attackers are stealing authenticated browser sessions from infected computers, enabling them to bypass passwords and two-factor authentication. Anthropic is signing affected users out of Claude, removing saved payment methods, and refunding unauthorised chargesIn an email sent to affected accounts, Anthropic said it recently became aware of a bad actor using common infostealer malware to steal Claude login sessions directly from people's computers, then using those stolen sessions to access accounts and burn through the victims' usage. The email, which was shared publicly on Reddit by one affected user, also gave people a way to recognise the symptom: if a Claude account's usage limits appeared to refill and then mysteriously drain while the account wasn't actively being used, that pattern was likely the cause.The mechanics of the attack make it particularly hard to notice. Infostealer malware can copy an already-authenticated browser session, meaning an attacker doesn't need to go through a normal password or two-factor authentication login process to gain access — they simply reuse a session that's already been verified.Anthropic said its investigation is still ongoing, but that affected computers were most likely already infected with general-purpose infostealer malware unrelated to Claude itself.The company was explicit on this point, stating it has no reason to believe the malware is connected to Claude, was installed through Claude, or relates to anything the user did within the Claude platform.According to Anthropic, this type of malware typically spreads through downloads or malicious apps, and once installed, harvests information stored locally on a device — including browser passwords, login cookies, and credentials tied to a wide range of other apps and services. A user's Claude session was likely just one of many pieces of data swept up in that broader collection process, with attackers only recently beginning to specifically extract and exploit the Claude sessions from what they'd already gathered.In the case shared on Reddit, the affected user confirmed they had downloaded a pirated game shortly before the compromise, offering a likely explanation for how the malware ended up on their system in the first place.Anthropic said it has identified several specific malware families involved in these attacks, including Vidar, LummaC2, StealC, RedLine, and Acreed on Windows systems, along with Atomic Stealer (AMOS) affecting a small number of Mac users.For accounts identified as compromised, Anthropic is taking several protective steps: signing affected users out of Claude, revoking the stolen sessions, removing any saved payment methods from the account, and refunding charges it identifies as unauthorized.However, the company was clear that this response only addresses the symptom, not the underlying cause. Anthropic warned that signing a user out stops the stolen session from being used, but it doesn't remove the malware itself — meaning if the infection is still present on a user's device, their very next login session could be stolen through the exact same method.Anthropic has urged affected users to take basic follow-up security steps beyond what the company can do on its end, including changing their account credentials, revoking any other active sessions tied to their accounts, and thoroughly removing the malware from their infected computers before logging back in.
Article Summary: AI giant Anthropic has issued a warning to Claude users after discovering that infostealer malware is hijacking active login sessions to access accounts and drain usage. Anthropic is signing affected users out of Claude, removing saved payment methods, and refunding unauthorised charges.

Article Title: VerSe Innovation launches SparkStation at Film Expo 2026
Article Text: VerSe Innovation has launched SparkStation at Film Expo 2026 - an AI content operating system that carries an entire production from first idea to final cut inside a single system. The company claims that SparkStation is VerSe's first global-first offering and one of the largest product bets the company has ever made. The platform is backed by $30+ million in committed investment over 24 months, spanning GPU infrastructure, proprietary AI orchestration, and specialist talent aiming to serve 100+ studios, 1,000+ brands and thousands of creators globally. Commercial models span credits for creators, seat-based SaaS for studios and brands, and enterprise licensing with API access.In a press release, the company stated that SparkStation rolls out in three phases: beta access (August 29), general availability (October 1), and enterprise API tier (November 1). It said that SparkStation is one platform built for three verticals:•Filmmakers and production houses: With capabilities that include, story builder, script coverage, casting, location design, storyboards, shot creation, music and dialogue generation, editing and rendering, with clean exports into industry-standard NLEs so that filmmakers retain control.•Brands, Businesses, E-commerce and Agencies: With image, video, UGC and performance ad formats, catalogue-scale product creative, and hundreds of localised, platform-reframed variants per campaign produced in hours rather than weeks.•Creators and influencers: With lots of templates and studio-grade output on a credits model.It delivers on five differentiators that compound:•An operating system, not a tool: Every stage of production in one pipeline. Unlike other platforms that generate mere clips, SparkStation delivers complete, coherent, continuous & consistent creative outputs.•Production-grade continuity across 5 locked elements: Face, expression, wardrobe, location & props, held across an entire production rather than a single shot. Continuity is the precise reason AI video has not crossed into professional workflows & SparkStation solves all of these 5 elements.•Model-agnostic orchestration: SparkStation routes each task - a face, a crowd, a camera move, a voice, a language to whichever model is best at it. Multiple models from every major provider sit behind one interface and each creative task is routed to the one that's best at it.•60+ languages at production fidelity: The performance travels and not just the words - lip movements, emotional beats and local idioms. Six weeks of localisation becomes one day.•Built by creators, for creators: Designed by a team drawn from film, VFX and gaming as much as from AI research with no lock-in and native exports to Premiere, Final Cut and DaVinci Resolve. Studios integrate with the NLEs while maintaining continuity across multi-language films. Brands produce infinite creative variants at fraction of traditional timelines. Agencies scale client deliverables. Creators access a full-service studio without infrastructure overhead.Umang Bedi, Co-Founder & CEO, VerSe Innovation, said “SparkStation is VerSe's first global offering and one of the single largest product bets VerSe has made. Production cost has been the invisible ceiling on what stories get made. When you solve that constraint, you don't simply make content cheaper. You make content that never cleared the production threshold before. That is what we are solving for - not efficiency, but possibility. SparkStation has been used internally for over 6 months now at scale delivering unprecedented speed and economics. Spark is not a platform in testing it is in production, at scale, generating revenue”.
Article Summary: SparkStation is VerSe's first global-first offering and one of the largest product bets the company has ever made. The platform is backed by $30+ million in committed investment over 24 months. It will serve 100+ studios, 1,000+ brands and thousands of creators globally.

Article Title: HP unveils DesignJet XT870 large-format printer at Photo Video Asia 2026: Price, features and more

HP DesignJet XT870 24-inch large format printer: Price and availability

HP DesignJet XT870 24-inch large format printer features

HP has expanded its product lineup with the launch of HP DesignJet XT870 24-inch large format printer at Photo Video Asia 2026.
